8.4.4. iLock_Geography.geo_algorithms.area.generateArea¶

iLock_Geography.geo_algorithms.area.generateArea(subtype, name, graph, delimUserTypes, nodes=None, edges=None, isDelimiting=None)¶

Iteratively enlarge area implicitly defined by the nodes and edges.

The area is enlarged edge by edge, skipping the edges that have a start node containing an object of any user type listed in delimUserTypes.

Note that it is not necessary that nodes belonging to edges in edges are members of nodes; those that are missing are automatically added.

Parameters:
  • subtype (str) – The usertype of the area to be enlarged.
  • name (str) – The name of the area to be enlarged.
  • graph (IGraph) – The traversal graph containing the nodes and edges.
  • delimUserTypes (Iterable(str)) – The user types that halt enlargement from the node. If a node contains an object of any user type in delimUserTypes, no enlargement will continue from that node.
  • nodes (Iterable(INode) | none) – The start collection of nodes. None means the empty set.
  • edges (Iterable(IEdge) | none) – The start collection of edges. None means the empty set. End points of edges do not need to be members in nodes; they are inferred.
  • isDelimiting (function | none) – Callback that maps (railyard object, index) to bool. Should return True if the given object having user type in c{delimUserTypes} should delimit the area assuming it is approached from the given index.
Return type:

IGraph
Returns:

The maximally enlarged area generated from the given “sub-area”.
